1	# Guest game and GitHub admin PWA release
2	
3	Current operator scope, 28 October 2026. This document supersedes the public
4	OpenAI sign-in, public PWA installation and browser role-delegation portions of
5	the earlier designs. QBrain is authoritative; this is its linked implementation
6	and verification projection. Implementation and hosted rollout are in progress.
7	
8	## Behavior and boundaries
9	
10	The public game accepts guests only. Generated aliases, icons, browser-persistent
11	guest credentials, rooms, private live updates and reactions remain available.
12	Public OpenAI login/callback routes return404. Public session responses expose no
13	administration permissions, stored/bootstrap grants do not elevate guests, and
14	member-shaped public sessions are rejected. Community suggestion/nomination UI
15	and the former `/content` entry are inactive in this release.
16	
17	Administration uses the registered [Word Pairs Admin GitHub App](https://github.com/settings/apps/word-pairs-admin-sharpninja).
18	Only verified GitHub numeric account16146732 and login `sharpninja` can complete
19	sign-in. The private App requests no repository, organization or email permissions
20	and has no webhook. User-access delegation is disabled: `/admin/users` redirects
21	to `/admin` and its API returns404 without touching access storage. Existing ACL
22	and community policy/domain/history remain preserved for future scope.
23	
24	Server configuration uses `WORDPAIRS_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID` and
25	`WORDPAIRS_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET`, never public-prefixed variables. Both callback
26	URLs are registered exactly:
27	
28	- `https://wordpairs.vercel.app/api/auth/github/callback` (staging).
29	- `https://wordpairs-j9jf.vercel.app/api/auth/github/callback` (production).
30	
31	The provider uses Authorization Code with S256PKCE and state. Existing persisted
32	challenges are browser-bound, expire after10minutes and are consumed before
33	callback validation. The server exchanges the code and verifies `/user`; it
34	retains neither GitHub access/refresh tokens nor provider email. Admin cookies
35	`wp_admin`/`wp_admin_login` and stored hashes have a separate `github-admin` purpose
36	namespace from `wp_session`. Copying a guest token into an admin cookie or the
37	reverse cannot authenticate. Admin login/logout leaves the guest session intact.
38	Admin responses are private/no-store; logout requires the canonical same origin.
39	
40	## Installation and offline behavior
41	
42	Only the admin layout links `/admin/manifest.webmanifest`. Its stable identity,
43	start URL and scope are `/admin`; display is standalone and its name is Wordpairs
44	Admin. Existing opaque192/512 PNGs, maskable icon and Apple touch icon are reused.
45	The manifest is an explicit route because nested `admin/manifest.ts` is not a
46	recognized metadata convention in the installed Next.js version.
47	
48	Authenticated admin UI offers installation and phone instructions. It registers
49	`/admin-sw.js` with scope `/admin`, `updateViaCache: none`, no-store script headers
50	and `Service-Worker-Allowed: /admin`. The worker handles only same-origin GET
51	admin document navigation. HTTP errors pass through; a network failure receives
52	the generic `/admin-offline.html` reconnect/sign-in screen. API/auth/RSC requests,
53	mutations and public game navigation receive no offline fallback. No operation
54	is queued for later execution.
55	
56	Only the offline document and four public icons are cached under
57	`wordpairs-admin-pwa-v1`. Sessions, profiles, admin HTML, answers, room projections,
58	credentials and mutation responses are never put in CacheStorage. Normal admin
59	updates wait for active clients and delete only older admin cache versions.
60	
61	Public pages have no manifest or install controls. The former `/sw.js` remains
62	as a retirement worker with no fetch handler; it deletes only `wordpairs-pwa-*`
63	caches and unregisters itself. Root cleanup recognizes only that exact former
64	root registration and cache prefix, preserving admin and unrelated apps. Website
65	code cannot remove an existing OS home-screen icon or prevent browser bookmarks.
66	
67	## Traceability and repeatable cases
68	
69	QBrain records: `FR-GUESTADMIN-031`, `TR-GITHUB-ADMIN-043`,
70	`TEST-GITHUBADMIN-149`; updated existing `FR-IDENTITY-018`,
71	`FR-PLAYERPROFILE-002`, `FR-ADMINPAGES-023`, `FR-PHONEINSTALL-026`,
72	`TR-IDENTITY-AUTHENTICATION-016`, `TR-PWA-INSTALLATION-036`,
73	`TR-PWA-CACHEPRIVACY-037`, `TEST-ADMINUI-136`, `TEST-PWAINSTALL-137`,
74	`TEST-PWAPRIVACY-138` and `TEST-IDENTITYAUTHENTICATION-116`. Native mappings
75	preserve prior edges. Changed criteria remain unsatisfied until their new evidence
76	and independent review justify a separate status update.
77	
78	- `FR-GUESTADMIN-031#GA-01/02` maps public guest-only behavior and disabled secured
79	  entry to identity/content/admin HTTP tests and the rendered navigation/content
80	  browser journeys. Original multi-account community UI cases are retained in
81	  `docs/testing/historical/*.spec.ts.txt`; inactive features are not silently
82	  represented as current successful UI coverage. Domain/transaction tests remain.
83	- `FR-GUESTADMIN-031#GA-03/04/08` and `TR-GITHUB-ADMIN-043#GA-03/04/08` map to
84	  `TEST-GITHUBADMIN-149` and `TEST-ADMINUI-136`. Provider fakes cover wrong numeric
85	  ID, wrong login, malformed state/PKCE, denied/token/network failures and claim
86	  minimization. Actual runtime/repository composition tests cover token namespace
87	  isolation, stripped guest grants and separate logout. HTTP tests cover cookies,
88	  malformed callback parameters, CSRF and private responses. Rendered pages test
89	  direct guest denial, safe callback feedback, logout, stale responses and retries.
90	- `FR-PHONEINSTALL-026#PWA-01..05` and `TR-PWA-INSTALLATION-036` map to
91	  `TEST-PWAINSTALL-137`: inspect actual production HTML/manifest/icons; await real
92	  worker activation; inspect unfiltered Chromium installability diagnostics using
93	  a disposable regular profile; exercise click-only prompts and standalone hiding.
94	- `FR-PHONEINSTALL-026#PWA-06..09`, `TR-PWA-CACHEPRIVACY-037` and
95	  `FR-GUESTADMIN-031#GA-05..07` map to `TEST-PWAPRIVACY-138`: inspect the actual
96	  static cache allowlist, abort the real worker's outgoing network request, require
97	  a fresh admin URL response from that worker, assert generic offline content and failed private/API/public
98	  requests, reconnect and require authentication again. Deterministic worker and
99	  client tests preserve unrelated registrations/caches during legacy retirement.
100	- `FR-GUESTADMIN-031#GA-09` maps welcome/profile card whitespace to actual
101	 390px/1440px browser geometry and screenshots. Responsive padding is20px minimum
102	  on phones and32px on desktop, with no horizontal overflow.
103	
104	`TEST-GITHUBADMIN-149` objective is to prove that guest gameplay cannot grant
105	administration and that only the verified owner flow creates a usable admin
106	session. Priority is critical. Preconditions are an isolated database/network
107	adapter or declared HTTP fixture and independent guest/admin browser contexts.
108	Data includes owner numeric ID16146732, wrong ID16146733, wrong login, unique
109	opaque browser tokens, duplicate callback parameters and synthetic catalog cases.
110	Use phone390x844 and desktop1440x900, plus the existing enlargement/orientation
111	matrix. Never use live users or actual provider tokens as fixture data.
112	
113	Ordered actions and expected observations:
114	
115	1. Open public play, continue as guest, and attempt admin entry with only the
116	   guest credential. Guest play works; no public provider/install/delegation links
117	   appear; private APIs deny before reading records.
118	2. Complete a fixed-owner provider fixture, then try wrong ID/login, bad state,
119	   missing/expired/consumed challenge and malformed callbacks. Only the verified
120	   owner path may issue `wp_admin`; failures show safe feedback and no private UI.
121	3. Copy each issued opaque token into the other realm's cookie. Both copies fail.
122	   Sign out of admin with a same-origin request; only its stored session/cookie
123	   is revoked. A cross-origin request changes nothing.
124	4. Open admin word/hint forms, save/retry an uncertain write, and deny a mutation
125	   while an old read is pending. Existing versions/audit remain immutable, the
126	   command is reused without duplicates, and old responses cannot restore data.
127	5. Inspect installation metadata and activate the real admin worker; abort
128	   its outgoing network request and navigate to a fresh admin URL. Only a static reconnect screen appears.
129	   Reconnect and verify current authentication, never cached private content.
130	
131	Synchronization is condition-based: await responses, visible states, cache
132	contents and worker activation, without fixed sleeps. Cleanup closes owned
133	contexts/profiles and resets only disposable fixture resources. Automation is
134	ready through the named Vitest and Playwright suites; HTTP fixture evidence does
135	not establish live GitHub consent or phone OS installation.
136	
137	The offline browser case routes and aborts only service-worker-owned outgoing
138	network requests before enabling browser offline mode for subsequent API/public
139	checks. Chromium offline emulation alone intermittently left worker fetches online.
140	The case requires an actual worker response and records the intercepted request;
141	it never supplies mocked fallback HTML. This uses Playwright's documented
142	[service worker network routing](https://playwright.dev/docs/service-workers).
143	
144	```gherkin
145	Scenario: TEST-GITHUBADMIN-149 owner administration is isolated from guest play
146	  Given a browser has a valid guest session with stored administrator role data
147	  When it requests the administration session using only that guest token
148	  Then no administrator profile is returned
149	  And no private catalog records are read
150	  When GitHub identifies numeric account 16146733 with login sharpninja
151	  Then the callback creates no administrator session
152	  When GitHub identifies numeric account 16146732 with login sharpninja
153	  And its browser-bound challenge is current and unused
154	  Then only the administrator session cookie is issued
155	  And the existing guest session cookie is unchanged
156	  When the administrator signs out
157	  Then its stored administrator session is revoked
158	  And the guest session remains usable
159	```
160	
161	## Verification, operations and open dependencies
162	
163	Use `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, then production-browser
164	`npx playwright test --config=playwright.pwa.config.ts`. The full active browser
165	suite includes all currently enabled guest/game/admin flows. Source-level provider
166	and namespace tests are `tests/integration/github-admin.test.ts` and
167	`tests/integration/admin-session-isolation.test.ts`; HTTP checks include
168	`tests/web/github-admin-api.test.ts`. No new database migration or package is
169	needed for this release. Existing schema and private Realtime/scheduler remain
170	separate deployment prerequisites.
171	
172	Real PostgreSQL coverage in `tests/integration/admin.integration.ts` exercises the
173	actual login/callback/session/content routes and runtime composition, with only
174	the external GitHub transport faked. It verifies stored one-time challenges,
175	cross-realm denial, catalog writes, callback replay and durable logout. Run the
176	full database suite with `tests/integration/run-phase1.ps1 -ReportDirectory <path>`;
177	`-VolatileStorage` uses an owned temporary PostgreSQL container and does not prove
178	disk durability or crash recovery. `scripts/Convert-JUnitToTrx.ps1` adapts each
179	native JUnit case into the review's TRX format, preserving original JUnit receipts.
180	TRX conversion timestamps are explicitly distinguished from execution times.
181	
182	The wider browser run also exposed a presence-timer regression:15-second profile
183	refreshes changed the profile object and restarted the20-second heartbeat effect.
184	Room refresh now depends on stable profile ID; the existing uncertain-readiness
185	browser case verifies repeated presence during a pending request. Artwork tests
186	now require absence of the removed public install panel and explicitly set their
187	desktop viewport instead of inheriting a phone viewport.
188	
189	Keep every failed test/build run and hostile-review round. Original admin ACL,
190	OpenAI and public-PWA receipts remain historical, not approval of these bytes.
191	The first architecture review rejected a nested manifest and missing callback
192	feedback; both findings require fresh final evidence. Final source review is
193	Claude Opus, explicitly selected by the operator. Real hosted GitHub consent,
194	standalone phone OAuth cookie continuity and physical OS installation remain
195	distinct from fixture/browser installability evidence. Deployment claims must
196	name the actual reviewed source commit and verified public endpoint.

callback validation. The server exchanges the code and verifies `/user`; it
retains neither GitHub access/refresh tokens nor provider email. Admin cookies
`wp_admin`/`wp_admin_login` and stored hashes have a separate `github-admin` purpose
namespace from `wp_session`. Copying a guest token into an admin cookie or the
reverse cannot authenticate. Admin login/logout leaves the guest session intact.
Admin responses are private/no-store; logout requires the canonical same origin.

## Installation and offline behavior

Only the admin layout links `/admin/manifest.webmanifest`. Its stable identity,
start URL and scope are `/admin`; display is standalone and its name is Wordpairs
Admin. Existing opaque192/512 PNGs, maskable icon and Apple touch icon are reused.
The manifest is an explicit route because nested `admin/manifest.ts` is not a
recognized metadata convention in the installed Next.js version.

Authenticated admin UI offers installation and phone instructions. It registers
`/admin-sw.js` with scope `/admin`, `updateViaCache: none`, no-store script headers
and `Service-Worker-Allowed: /admin`. The worker handles only same-origin GET
admin document navigation. HTTP errors pass through; a network failure receives
the generic `/admin-offline.html` reconnect/sign-in screen. API/auth/RSC requests,
mutations and public game navigation receive no offline fallback. No operation
is queued for later execution.

Only the offline document and four public icons are cached under
`wordpairs-admin-pwa-v1`. Sessions, profiles, admin HTML, answers, room projections,
credentials and mutation responses are never put in CacheStorage. Normal admin
updates wait for active clients and delete only older admin cache versions.

Public pages have no manifest or install controls. The former `/sw.js` remains
as a retirement worker with no fetch handler; it deletes only `wordpairs-pwa-*`
caches and unregisters itself. Root cleanup recognizes only that exact former
root registration and cache prefix, preserving admin and unrelated apps. Website
code cannot remove an existing OS home-screen icon or prevent browser bookmarks.

## Traceability and repeatable cases

QBrain records: `FR-GUESTADMIN-031`, `TR-GITHUB-ADMIN-043`,
`TEST-GITHUBADMIN-149`; updated existing `FR-IDENTITY-018`,
`FR-PLAYERPROFILE-002`, `FR-ADMINPAGES-023`, `FR-PHONEINSTALL-026`,
`TR-IDENTITY-AUTHENTICATION-016`, `TR-PWA-INSTALLATION-036`,
`TR-PWA-CACHEPRIVACY-037`, `TEST-ADMINUI-136`, `TEST-PWAINSTALL-137`,
`TEST-PWAPRIVACY-138` and `TEST-IDENTITYAUTHENTICATION-116`. Native mappings
preserve prior edges. Changed criteria remain unsatisfied until their new evidence
and independent review justify a separate status update.

- `FR-GUESTADMIN-031#GA-01/02` maps public guest-only behavior and disabled secured
  entry to identity/content/admin HTTP tests and the rendered navigation/content
  browser journeys. Original multi-account community UI cases are retained in
  `docs/testing/historical/*.spec.ts.txt`; inactive features are not silently
  represented as current successful UI coverage. Domain/transaction tests remain.
- `FR-GUESTADMIN-031#GA-03/04/08` and `TR-GITHUB-ADMIN-043#GA-03/04/08` map to
  `TEST-GITHUBADMIN-149` and `TEST-ADMINUI-136`. Provider fakes cover wrong numeric
  ID, wrong login, malformed state/PKCE, denied/token/network failures and claim
  minimization. Actual runtime/repository composition tests cover token namespace
  isolation, stripped guest grants and separate logout. HTTP tests cover cookies,
  malformed callback parameters, CSRF and private responses. Rendered pages test
  direct guest denial, safe callback feedback, logout, stale responses and retries.
- `FR-PHONEINSTALL-026#PWA-01..05` and `TR-PWA-INSTALLATION-036` map to
  `TEST-PWAINSTALL-137`: inspect actual production HTML/manifest/icons; await real
  worker activation; inspect unfiltered Chromium installability diagnostics using
  a disposable regular profile; exercise click-only prompts and standalone hiding.
- `FR-PHONEINSTALL-026#PWA-06..09`, `TR-PWA-CACHEPRIVACY-037` and
  `FR-GUESTADMIN-031#GA-05..07` map to `TEST-PWAPRIVACY-138`: inspect the actual
  static cache allowlist, abort the real worker's outgoing network request, require
  a fresh admin URL response from that worker, assert generic offline content and failed private/API/public
  requests, reconnect and require authentication again. Deterministic worker and
  client tests preserve unrelated registrations/caches during legacy retirement.
- `FR-GUESTADMIN-031#GA-09` maps welcome/profile card whitespace to actual
 390px/1440px browser geometry and screenshots. Responsive padding is20px minimum
  on phones and32px on desktop, with no horizontal overflow.

`TEST-GITHUBADMIN-149` objective is to prove that guest gameplay cannot grant
administration and that only the verified owner flow creates a usable admin
session. Priority is critical. Preconditions are an isolated database/network
adapter or declared HTTP fixture and independent guest/admin browser contexts.
Data includes owner numeric ID16146732, wrong ID16146733, wrong login, unique
opaque browser tokens, duplicate callback parameters and synthetic catalog cases.
Use phone390x844 and desktop1440x900, plus the existing enlargement/orientation
matrix. Never use live users or actual provider tokens as fixture data.

Ordered actions and expected observations:

1. Open public play, continue as guest, and attempt admin entry with only the
   guest credential. Guest play works; no public provider/install/delegation links
   appear; private APIs deny before reading records.
2. Complete a fixed-owner provider fixture, then try wrong ID/login, bad state,
   missing/expired/consumed challenge and malformed callbacks. Only the verified
   owner path may issue `wp_admin`; failures show safe feedback and no private UI.
3. Copy each issued opaque token into the other realm's cookie. Both copies fail.
   Sign out of admin with a same-origin request; only its stored session/cookie
   is revoked. A cross-origin request changes nothing.
4. Open admin word/hint forms, save/retry an uncertain write, and deny a mutation
   while an old read is pending. Existing versions/audit remain immutable, the
   command is reused without duplicates, and old responses cannot restore data.
5. Inspect installation metadata and activate the real admin worker; abort
   its outgoing network request and navigate to a fresh admin URL. Only a static reconnect screen appears.
   Reconnect and verify current authentication, never cached private content.

Synchronization is condition-based: await responses, visible states, cache
contents and worker activation, without fixed sleeps. Cleanup closes owned
contexts/profiles and resets only disposable fixture resources. Automation is
ready through the named Vitest and Playwright suites; HTTP fixture evidence does
not establish live GitHub consent or phone OS installation.

The offline browser case routes and aborts only service-worker-owned outgoing
network requests before enabling browser offline mode for subsequent API/public
checks. Chromium offline emulation alone intermittently left worker fetches online.
The case requires an actual worker response and records the intercepted request;
it never supplies mocked fallback HTML. This uses Playwright's documented
[service worker network routing](https://playwright.dev/docs/service-workers).

```gherkin
Scenario: TEST-GITHUBADMIN-149 owner administration is isolated from guest play
  Given a browser has a valid guest session with stored administrator role data
  When it requests the administration session using only that guest token
  Then no administrator profile is returned
  And no private catalog records are read
  When GitHub identifies numeric account 16146733 with login sharpninja
  Then the callback creates no administrator session
  When GitHub identifies numeric account 16146732 with login sharpninja
  And its browser-bound challenge is current and unused
  Then only the administrator session cookie is issued
  And the existing guest session cookie is unchanged
  When the administrator signs out
  Then its stored administrator session is revoked
  And the guest session remains usable
```

## Verification, operations and open dependencies

Use `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, then production-browser
`npx playwright test --config=playwright.pwa.config.ts`. The full active browser
suite includes all currently enabled guest/game/admin flows. Source-level provider
and namespace tests are `tests/integration/github-admin.test.ts` and
`tests/integration/admin-session-isolation.test.ts`; HTTP checks include
`tests/web/github-admin-api.test.ts`. No new database migration or package is
needed for this release. Existing schema and private Realtime/scheduler remain
separate deployment prerequisites.

Real PostgreSQL coverage in `tests/integration/admin.integration.ts` exercises the
actual login/callback/session/content routes and runtime composition, with only
the external GitHub transport faked. It verifies stored one-time challenges,
cross-realm denial, catalog writes, callback replay and durable logout. Run the
full database suite with `tests/integration/run-phase1.ps1 -ReportDirectory <path>`;
`-VolatileStorage` uses an owned temporary PostgreSQL container and does not prove
disk durability or crash recovery. `scripts/Convert-JUnitToTrx.ps1` adapts each
native JUnit case into the review's TRX format, preserving original JUnit receipts.
TRX conversion timestamps are explicitly distinguished from execution times.

The wider browser run also exposed a presence-timer regression:15-second profile
refreshes changed the profile object and restarted the20-second heartbeat effect.
Room refresh now depends on stable profile ID; the existing uncertain-readiness
browser case verifies repeated presence during a pending request. Artwork tests
now require absence of the removed public install panel and explicitly set their
desktop viewport instead of inheriting a phone viewport.

Keep every failed test/build run and hostile-review round. Original admin ACL,
OpenAI and public-PWA receipts remain historical, not approval of these bytes.
The first architecture review rejected a nested manifest and missing callback
feedback; both findings require fresh final evidence. Final source review is
Claude Opus, explicitly selected by the operator. Real hosted GitHub consent,
standalone phone OAuth cookie continuity and physical OS installation remain
distinct from fixture/browser installability evidence. Deployment claims must
name the actual reviewed source commit and verified public endpoint.

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$ws = '[HOME]/github/WordGame/.mcpServer/wordpairs'

$request = Get-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $ws 'docs/receipts/hv/20261028T195803-admin-pwa-source-round1.request.jsonl') -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
$ns = 'http://microsoft.com/schemas/VisualStudio/TeamTest/2010'
Write-Output ("ADAPTER-SHA256: {0}" -f (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath (Join-Path $ws 'scripts/Convert-JUnitToTrx.ps1') -Algorithm SHA256).Hash)
foreach ($e in $request.evidence) {
    $trxPath = [string]$e.path
    $name = [IO.Path]::GetFileNameWithoutExtension($trxPath)
    $xmlPath = Join-Path $dir ($name + '.xml')
    $hash = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $trxPath -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
    [xml]$trx = [IO.File]::ReadAllText($trxPath)
    $m = [Xml.XmlNamespaceManager]::new($trx.NameTable); $m.AddNamespace('t', $ns)
    $results = @($trx.SelectNodes('//t:UnitTestResult', $m))
    $counters = $trx.SelectSingleNode('//t:Counters', $m)
    $outcomes = $results | Group-Object { $_.GetAttribute('outcome') } | ForEach-Object { '{0}={1}' -f $_.Name, $_.Count }
    $runText = $trx.SelectSingleNode('//t:RunInfo/t:Text', $m).InnerText
    $times = $trx.SelectSingleNode('//t:Times', $m)
    [xml]$junit = [IO.File]::ReadAllText($xmlPath)
    $cases = @($junit.SelectNodes('//testcase'))
    $jFail = @($junit.SelectNodes('//testcase[failure or error]')).Count
    $jSkip = @($junit.SelectNodes('//testcase[skipped]')).Count
    $root = $junit.DocumentElement
    $jHash = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $xmlPath -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
    $trxNames = @($results | ForEach-Object { $_.GetAttribute('testName') })
    $junitNames = @($cases | ForEach-Object { $_.GetAttribute('classname') + ' :: ' + $_.GetAttribute('name') })
    $diff = @(Compare-Object -ReferenceObject $junitNames -DifferenceObject $trxNames -SyncWindow 0)
    $dupes = @($junitNames | Group-Object | Where-Object Count -gt 1)
    $suiteTs = @($junit.SelectNodes('//testsuite') | ForEach-Object { $_.GetAttribute('timestamp') } | Where-Object { $_ } | Sort-Object -Unique)
    Write-Output ("== {0}" -f $name)
    Write-Output ("  trxSha256={0} requestSha256={1} match={2}" -f $hash, $e.sha256, ($hash -eq $e.sha256))
    Write-Output ("  trxResults={0} requestCases={1} counters total={2} passed={3} failed={4} notExecuted={5} outcomes=[{6}]" -f $results.Count, $e.cases, $counters.total, $counters.passed, $counters.failed, $counters.notExecuted, ($outcomes -join ','))
    Write-Output ("  junitRoot={0} tests={1} failures={2} errors={3} skipped={4} testcaseNodes={5} failNodes={6} skipNodes={7} rootTimestamp={8}" -f $root.Name, $root.GetAttribute('tests'), $root.GetAttribute('failures'), $root.GetAttribute('errors'), $root.GetAttribute('skipped'), $cases.Count, $jFail, $jSkip, $root.GetAttribute('timestamp'))
    Write-Output ("  suiteTimestamps={0}" -f ($suiteTs -join ' | '))
    Write-Output ("  nameOrderDiffs={0} duplicateJUnitNames={1} trxTimesStart={2}" -f $diff.Count, $dupes.Count, $times.GetAttribute('start'))
    $declared = [regex]::Match($runText, 'SHA256=([0-9A-F]{64})').Groups[1].Value
    $rev = [regex]::Match($runText, 'reviewed revision=([0-9a-f]{40})').Groups[1].Value
    Write-Output ("  trxDeclaresJUnitSha={0} actualJUnitSha={1} match={2} declaredRevision={3}" -f $declared, $jHash, ($declared -eq $jHash), $rev)
    foreach ($d in $dupes | Select-Object -First 5) { Write-Output ("  DUP: {0} x{1}" -f $d.Name, $d.Count) }
}

    $jHash = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $xmlPath -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
    $trxNames = @($results | ForEach-Object { $_.GetAttribute('testName') })
    $junitNames = @($cases | ForEach-Object { $_.GetAttribute('classname') + ' :: ' + $_.GetAttribute('name') })
    $diff = @(Compare-Object -ReferenceObject $junitNames -DifferenceObject $trxNames -SyncWindow 0)
    $dupes = @($junitNames | Group-Object | Where-Object Count -gt 1)
    $suiteTs = @($junit.SelectNodes('//testsuite') | ForEach-Object { $_.GetAttribute('timestamp') } | Where-Object { $_ } | Sort-Object -Unique)
    Write-Output ("== {0}" -f $name)
    Write-Output ("  trxSha256={0} requestSha256={1} match={2}" -f $hash, $e.sha256, ($hash -eq $e.sha256))
    Write-Output ("  trxResults={0} requestCases={1} counters total={2} passed={3} failed={4} notExecuted={5} outcomes=[{6}]" -f $results.Count, $e.cases, $counters.total, $counters.passed, $counters.failed, $counters.notExecuted, ($outcomes -join ','))
    Write-Output ("  junitRoot={0} tests={1} failures={2} errors={3} skipped={4} testcaseNodes={5} failNodes={6} skipNodes={7} rootTimestamp={8}" -f $root.Name, $root.GetAttribute('tests'), $root.GetAttribute('failures'), $root.GetAttribute('errors'), $root.GetAttribute('skipped'), $cases.Count, $jFail, $jSkip, $root.GetAttribute('timestamp'))
    Write-Output ("  suiteTimestamps={0}" -f ($suiteTs -join ' | '))
    Write-Output ("  nameOrderDiffs={0} duplicateJUnitNames={1} trxTimesStart={2}" -f $diff.Count, $dupes.Count, $times.GetAttribute('start'))
    $declared = [regex]::Match($runText, 'SHA256=([0-9A-F]{64})').Groups[1].Value
    $rev = [regex]::Match($runText, 'reviewed revision=([0-9a-f]{40})').Groups[1].Value
    Write-Output ("  trxDeclaresJUnitSha={0} actualJUnitSha={1} match={2} declaredRevision={3}" -f $declared, $jHash, ($declared -eq $jHash), $rev)
    foreach ($d in $dupes | Select-Object -First 5) { Write-Output ("  DUP: {0} x{1}" -f $d.Name, $d.Count) }
}

1	---
2	name: Requirements Management
3	description: Use when the user asks to "list requirements", "add requirement", "create FR", "create TR", "create test requirement", "generate requirements document", or "ingest requirements".
4	version: 0.1.0
5	---
6	
7	# Requirements Management
8	
9	## Overview
10	
11	To manage functional requirements (FR), technical requirements (TR), test requirements (TEST), and their traceability mappings, use this plugin's declared hook/wrapper (or the REPL transport) for the `workflow.requirements.*` namespace. Do not substitute raw REST calls, generic `PowerShell.MCP wrapper`, helper modules, or another agent's plugin for normal requirements work.
12	
13	The plugin wrapper validates documented params and emits single-line JSON to REPL stdio. Any direct REPL diagnostic call must use one single-line JSON request envelope, not formatted YAML.
14	
15	The database is the source of truth for requirements. Markdown files are import/export projections only. Every operation is scoped to the workspace resolved from the signed marker, and generated workspace output must contain only the requested workspace's FR, TR, TEST, and traceability links.
16	
17	## Initialization
18	
19	Call `workflow.sessionlog.bootstrap` through this plugin's declared hook/wrapper to initialize the session log subsystem before issuing any workflow commands. This call is idempotent and should be made once per conversation context.
20	
21	```yaml
22	type: request
23	payload:
24	  requestId: req-20260409T120000Z-bootstrap-001
25	  method: workflow.sessionlog.bootstrap
26	  params: {}
27	```
28	
29	## Requirement Scope Layers
30	
31	Plugin version 1.13.0 and newer exposes native layer operations. Treat this section as the layer API reference when plugin status reports these methods; do not ask the operator or inspect wrapper source just to learn the parameter shapes.
32	
33	- `workflow.requirements.listLayers` / `req_list_layers` / `client.Requirements.ListRequirementLayersAsync`: omit params.
34	- `workflow.requirements.createLayer` / `req_create_layer` / `client.Requirements.CreateRequirementLayerAsync`: required params are `key`, `order`, and `name`; optional params are `description` and `scopeEndLayerKey`.
35	- `workflow.requirements.updateLayer` / `req_update_layer` / `client.Requirements.UpdateRequirementLayerAsync`: required param is `key`; optional params are `name`, `description`, and `scopeEndLayerKey`. Layer `order` is immutable; create a new layer rather than attempting to update `order`.
36	- `workflow.requirements.effective` / `req_effective` / `client.Requirements.GetEffectiveRequirementsAsync`: optional param is `layerKey`; omit `layerKey` to use the active workspace layer.
37	
38	Use camelCase exactly in YAML:
39	
40	```yaml
41	type: request
42	payload:
43	  requestId: req-20260409T115900Z-listlayers-001
44	  method: workflow.requirements.listLayers
45	  params: {}
46	```
47	
48	```yaml
49	type: request
50	payload:
51	  requestId: req-20260409T115901Z-createlayer-001
52	  method: workflow.requirements.createLayer
53	  params:
54	    key: future
55	    order: 20
56	    name: Future Layer
57	    description: Requirements that are documented but not currently enforceable
58	```
59	
60	```yaml
61	type: request
62	payload:
63	  requestId: req-20260409T115902Z-updatelayer-001
64	  method: workflow.requirements.updateLayer
65	  params:
66	    key: future
67	    name: Future Layer
68	    scopeEndLayerKey: release
69	```
70	
71	```yaml
72	type: request
73	payload:
74	  requestId: req-20260409T115903Z-effective-001
75	  method: workflow.requirements.effective
76	  params:
77	    layerKey: future
78	```
79	
80	FR, TR, TEST, and batch create/update commands also accept requirement scope fields:
81	
82	- `scopeStartLayerKey`: first layer where the requirement is effective.
83	- `scopeEndLayerKey`: last layer where the requirement is effective; omit for open-ended scope.
84	
85	Omit both fields for requirements that are effective in the default/current layer.
86	
87	## Requirement ID Conventions
88	
89	Three ID spaces are in use:
90	
91	- **FR** - Functional Requirements: `^FR-[A-Z]+-\d{3}$`, e.g. `FR-MCP-001`, `FR-AUTH-042`
92	- **TR** - Technical Requirements: `^TR-[A-Z]+-[A-Z]+-\d{3}$`, e.g. `TR-MCP-ARCH-001`, `TR-AUTH-SEC-002`
93	- **TEST** - Test Requirements: `^TEST-[A-Z]+-\d{3}$`, e.g. `TEST-MCP-001`, `TEST-AUTH-003`
94	
95	All IDs must be uppercase. TR IDs require both an area and a subarea segment; FR and TEST IDs require only an area segment.
96	
97	## Functional Requirements (FR)
98	
99	### Listing FRs
100	
101	To retrieve a filtered list of functional requirements:
102	
103	```yaml
104	type: request
105	payload:
106	  requestId: req-20260409T120000Z-listfr-001
107	  method: workflow.requirements.listFr
108	  params:
109	    area: MCP
110	    status: in_progress
111	```
112	
113	All params are optional; omit to return all FRs. The result contains an `items` array:
114	
115	```yaml
116	type: result
117	payload:
118	  requestId: req-20260409T120000Z-listfr-001
119	  result:
120	    items:
121	      - id: FR-MCP-001
122	        title: Agent authentication
123	        description: System must authenticate AI agents via API key
124	        status: completed
125	        priority: critical
126	        area: MCP
127	        createdAt: 2026-03-01T10:00:00Z
128	        updatedAt: 2026-04-09T12:00:00Z
129	    totalCount: 1
130	```
131	
132	Valid `status` values: `pending`, `in_progress`, `completed`, `deferred`.
133	
134	### Getting a Single FR
135	
136	To fetch one functional requirement by ID:
137	
138	```yaml
139	type: request
140	payload:
141	  requestId: req-20260409T120001Z-getfr-001
142	  method: workflow.requirements.getFr
143	  params:
144	    id: FR-MCP-001
145	```
146	
147	### Creating an FR
148	
149	To record a new functional requirement:
150	
151	```yaml
152	type: request
153	payload:
154	  requestId: req-20260409T120002Z-createfr-001
155	  method: workflow.requirements.createFr
156	  params:
157	    id: FR-MCP-003
158	    title: Context search
159	    description: System must support semantic search across workspace documents
160	    priority: high
161	    area: MCP
162	    notes: Use hybrid search combining BM25 and vector embeddings
163	```
164	
165	Required fields: `id`, `title`, `description`, `priority`, `area`. The `notes` field is optional.
166	
167	### Acceptance Criteria
168	
169	FR, TR, and TEST create/update commands accept structured `acceptanceCriteria` entries with the same shape used by TODO execution criteria:
170	
171	```yaml
172	method: workflow.requirements.createFr
173	params:
174	  id: FR-MCP-XXX-001
175	  title: Acceptance criteria example
176	  description: Requirement records preserve structured pass/fail criteria.
177	  priority: high
178	  area: MCP
179	  acceptanceCriteria:
180	    - id: ac-1
181	      text: Round-trip preserves criterion text
182	      isSatisfied: false
183	    - id: ac-2
184	      text: Evidence is retained when supplied
185	      isSatisfied: true
186	      evidence: tests/Services/RequirementAcceptanceCriteriaTests.cs
187	```
188	
189	To copy criteria from an execution TODO onto a requirement, call `workflow.requirements.copyAcceptanceCriteriaFromTodo`:
190	
191	```yaml
192	method: workflow.requirements.copyAcceptanceCriteriaFromTodo
193	params:
194	  kind: fr
195	  id: FR-MCP-XXX-001
196	  todoId: PLAN-MCP-001
197	```
198	
199	This maps to `POST /mcpserver/requirements/{kind}/{id}/acceptance-criteria/copy-from-todo` with body `{ "todoId": "PLAN-MCP-001" }`.
200	
201	### Batch Create Or Update
202	
203	When creating or updating multiple records, prefer the atomic batch commands instead of Markdown ingestion. Batch commands accept YAML `records:` arrays and fail all records if any record is invalid, conflicts, or is missing during update.
204	
205	Use per-kind commands when every record is the same type:
206	
207	```yaml
208	type: request
209	payload:
210	  requestId: req-20260409T120002Z-createfr-batch-001
211	  method: workflow.requirements.createFrBatch
212	  params:
213	    records:
214	      - id: FR-MCP-004
215	        title: Batch requirements
216	        description: The system must accept multiple requirement records in one request.
217	        priority: high
218	      - id: FR-MCP-005
219	        title: Atomic validation
220	        description: The system must reject the whole batch when one record is invalid.
221	        priority: high
222	```
223	
224	Use `workflow.requirements.updateFrBatch`, `createTrBatch`, `updateTrBatch`, `createTestBatch`, and `updateTestBatch` for per-kind batches. For mixed FR/TR/TEST arrays, use `workflow.requirements.createBatch` or `workflow.requirements.updateBatch` and include `kind: fr|tr|test` on each record.
225	
226	### Updating an FR
227	
228	To modify an existing FR:
229	
230	```yaml
231	type: request
232	payload:
233	  requestId: req-20260409T120003Z-updatefr-001
234	  method: workflow.requirements.updateFr
235	  params:
236	    id: FR-MCP-003
237	    status: completed
238	    notes: Implemented with HybridSearchService using all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings
239	```
240	
241	### Deleting an FR
242	
243	```yaml
244	type: request
245	payload:
246	  requestId: req-20260409T120004Z-deletefr-001
247	  method: workflow.requirements.deleteFr
248	  params:
249	    id: FR-MCP-003
250	```
251	
252	## Technical Requirements (TR)
253	
254	TR IDs require both `area` and `subarea` segments. The full ID format is `TR-<AREA>-<SUBAREA>-###`.
255	
256	### Listing TRs
257	
258	```yaml
259	type: request
260	payload:
261	  requestId: req-20260409T120005Z-listtr-001
262	  method: workflow.requirements.listTr
263	  params:
264	    area: MCP
265	    subarea: PERF
266	```
267	
268	### Creating a TR
269	
270	```yaml
271	type: request
272	payload:
273	  requestId: req-20260409T120006Z-createtr-001
274	  method: workflow.requirements.createTr
275	  params:
276	    id: TR-MCP-PERF-001
277	    title: API response time SLA
278	    description: All API endpoints must respond within 500ms at p99
279	    priority: high
280	    area: MCP
281	    subarea: PERF
282	    notes: Measured at gateway, excluding network transit time
283	```
284	
285	### Updating a TR
286	
287	```yaml
288	type: request
289	payload:
290	  requestId: req-20260409T120007Z-updatetr-001
291	  method: workflow.requirements.updateTr
292	  params:
293	    id: TR-MCP-PERF-001
294	    status: in_progress
295	    notes: Baseline established at 320ms p99 under load test
296	```
297	
298	### Deleting a TR
299	
300	```yaml
301	type: request
302	payload:
303	  requestId: req-20260409T120008Z-deletetr-001
304	  method: workflow.requirements.deleteTr
305	  params:
306	    id: TR-MCP-PERF-001
307	```
308	
309	## Test Requirements (TEST)
310	
311	### Listing TEST Requirements
312	
313	```yaml
314	type: request
315	payload:
316	  requestId: req-20260409T120009Z-listtest-001
317	  method: workflow.requirements.listTest
318	  params:
319	    area: MCP
320	```
321	
322	### Creating a TEST Requirement
323	
324	```yaml
325	type: request
326	payload:
327	  requestId: req-20260409T120010Z-createtest-001
328	  method: workflow.requirements.createTest
329	  params:
330	    id: TEST-MCP-001
331	    title: Agent authentication unit test
332	    description: Verify API key authentication rejects invalid tokens with 401
333	    priority: critical
334	    area: MCP
335	    notes: Uses in-memory EF provider with CustomWebApplicationFactory
336	```
337	
338	### Updating and Deleting TEST Requirements
339	
340	Follow the same pattern as FR: use `workflow.requirements.updateTest` and `workflow.requirements.deleteTest` with the same parameter shapes.
341	
342	## Requirement Mappings
343	
344	Mappings link an FR to one or more TRs and TEST IDs in the current workspace, forming the traceability matrix.
345	
346	### Listing Mappings
347	
348	```yaml
349	type: request
350	payload:
351	  requestId: req-20260409T120011Z-listmap-001
352	  method: workflow.requirements.listMappings
353	  params:
354	    frId: FR-MCP-001
355	```
356	
357	### Creating a Mapping
358	
359	```yaml
360	type: request
361	payload:
362	  requestId: req-20260409T120012Z-createmap-001
363	  method: workflow.requirements.createMapping
364	  params:
365	    frId: FR-MCP-001
366	    trIds:
367	      - TR-MCP-ARCH-001
368	    testIds:
369	      - TEST-MCP-001
370	    notes: Core authentication flow covered by ARCH constraint and unit test
371	```
372	
373	Legacy single-link `trId` and `testId` inputs are accepted for compatibility. Prefer `trIds` and `testIds` for all new calls.
374	
375	The result confirms the stored mapping:
376	
377	```yaml
378	type: result
379	payload:
380	  requestId: req-20260409T120012Z-createmap-001
381	  result:
382	    item:
383	      frId: FR-MCP-001
384	      trId: TR-MCP-ARCH-001
385	      testId: TEST-MCP-001
386	      createdAt: 2026-04-09T12:00:12Z
387	      notes: Core authentication flow covered by ARCH constraint and unit test
388	```
389	
390	### Deleting a Mapping
391	
392	```yaml
393	type: request
394	payload:
395	  requestId: req-20260409T120013Z-deletemap-001
396	  method: workflow.requirements.deleteMapping
397	  params:
398	    frId: FR-MCP-001
399	    trId: TR-MCP-ARCH-001
400	```
401	
402	## Document Generation
403	
404	To generate formatted requirements documents from the current workspace database slice:
405	
406	```yaml
407	type: request
408	payload:
409	  requestId: req-20260409T120014Z-gendoc-001
410	  method: workflow.requirements.generateDocument
411	  params:
412	    format: markdown
413	    docType: matrix
414	```
415	
416	Valid `docType` values:
417	
418	- `functional` - numbered list of all FR entries with status and description
419	- `technical` - numbered list of all TR entries grouped by area/subarea
420	- `testing` - numbered list of all TEST entries with linked FR IDs
421	- `matrix` - traceability matrix table: FR × TR × TEST × status
422	- `all` - complete export package
423	
424	```yaml
425	type: result
426	payload:
427	  requestId: req-20260409T120014Z-gendoc-001
428	  result:
429	    content: |
430	      # Requirement Traceability Matrix
431	
432	      | FR ID      | TR ID           | TEST ID      | Status |
433	      |------------|-----------------|--------------|--------|
434	      | FR-MCP-001 | TR-MCP-ARCH-001 | TEST-MCP-001 | done   |
435	      | FR-MCP-002 | TR-MCP-ARCH-002 | TEST-MCP-003 | open   |
436	    format: markdown
437	    docType: matrix
438	    generatedAt: 2026-04-09T12:00:14Z
439	```
440	
441	### Wiki Export
442	
443	Use `format: wiki` with `docType: all` to export wiki files directly into the workspace. The normal result returns metadata, not archive bytes. Files are written under `docs/Project/wiki/azure` and `docs/Project/wiki/github`. Each folder includes `.mcp-requirements-manifest.json`; Azure also includes `.order`; GitHub also includes `_Sidebar.md` and `_Footer.md`. When an older REPL cannot serialize the metadata result, the wrapper may return `contentBase64` with `contentType: application/json`; decode it to read the same export metadata.
444	
445	```yaml
446	type: request
447	payload:
448	  requestId: req-20260409T120014Z-gendoc-wiki-001
449	  method: workflow.requirements.generateDocument
450	  params:
451	    format: wiki
452	    docType: all
453	```
454	
455	```yaml
456	type: result
457	payload:
458	  requestId: req-20260409T120014Z-gendoc-wiki-001
459	  result:
460	    format: wiki
461	    docType: all
462	    generatedAtUtc: 2026-04-09T12:00:14Z
463	    outputRoot: F:\GitHub\McpServer\docs\Project\wiki
464	    files:
465	      - relativePath: azure/Home.md
466	        fullPath: F:\GitHub\McpServer\docs\Project\wiki\azure\Home.md
467	        contentType: text/markdown
468	        lastModifiedUtc: 2026-04-09T12:00:14Z
469	```
470	
471	## Bulk Ingestion
472	
473	To import requirements from an existing Markdown document:
474	
475	```yaml
476	type: request
477	payload:
478	  requestId: req-20260409T120015Z-ingest-001
479	  method: workflow.requirements.ingestDocument
480	  params:
481	    content: |
482	      ## FR-MCP-010: GraphRAG ingestion
483	      The system must support ingestion of raw text into the GraphRAG corpus.
484	      Priority: high | Area: MCP | Status: pending
485	
486	      ## TR-MCP-GRAPH-001: Chunked text embedding
487	      Ingested text must be split into chunks and embedded using all-MiniLM-L6-v2.
488	      Priority: high | Area: MCP | Subarea: GRAPH | Status: pending
489	    format: markdown
490	```
491	
492	To import wiki documents, pass a path-keyed `documents` map and include `lastModifiedUtc` per entry when available. Use `sourceFormat: auto` or `wiki`; set `preferredWikiFormat: azure|github` only when the Azure and GitHub timestamp checks disagree. The server compares both `.mcp-requirements-manifest.json` `generatedAtUtc` values and the latest `lastModifiedUtc` per platform. If both checks agree, the newer platform is selected. If they disagree and no preference is supplied, import fails. The selected platform folder is authoritative: missing records are deleted, changed records are updated, new records are created, and identical records are ignored.
493	
494	```yaml
495	type: request
496	payload:
497	  requestId: req-20260409T120015Z-ingest-wiki-001
498	  method: workflow.requirements.ingestDocument
499	  params:
500	    format: wiki
501	    sourceFormat: wiki
502	    preferredWikiFormat: github
503	    documents:
504	      github/.mcp-requirements-manifest.json:
505	        content: '{"generatedAtUtc":"2026-04-09T12:00:14Z"}'
506	        lastModifiedUtc: 2026-04-09T12:00:14Z
507	      github/Functional-Requirements.md:
508	        content: |
509	          # Functional Requirements (MCP Server)
510	        lastModifiedUtc: 2026-04-09T12:00:15Z
511	```
512	
513	The server parses the document, creates, updates, deletes, or ignores matching FR/TR/TEST/mapping records, and returns a summary:
514	
515	```yaml
516	type: result
517	payload:
518	  requestId: req-20260409T120015Z-ingest-001
519	  result:
520	    created: 2
521	    updated: 0
522	    skipped: 0
523	    errors: []
524	```
525	
526	## Error Handling
527	
528	Common error codes:
529	
530	- `requirement_not_found` - no requirement with the given ID
531	- `requirement_already_exists` - ID already in use; update instead of create
532	- `invalid_requirement_id` - ID does not match the expected regex for its type
533	- `mapping_not_found` - mapping between the specified FR and TR does not exist
534	- `invalid_mapping` - mapping references a non-existent FR, TR, or TEST ID
535	- `document_generation_error` - failed to render the requested document format
536	- `document_ingestion_error` - could not parse or persist the ingested document
537	
538	## Workflow Recommendations
539	
540	When discovering or agreeing on new requirements during a session:
541	
542	1. Create the FR record immediately using `workflow.requirements.createFr`
543	2. Create the corresponding TR records using `workflow.requirements.createTr`
544	3. Create the TEST record using `workflow.requirements.createTest`
545	4. Link them with `workflow.requirements.createMapping`
546	5. Include the new IDs in the session log turn tags via `workflow.sessionlog.updateTurn`
547	
548	Capture requirements as they emerge; do not defer to end of session. Requirements traceability is validated in CI and build failures result from missing mappings.
549

---
name: Requirements Management
description: Use when the user asks to "list requirements", "add requirement", "create FR", "create TR", "create test requirement", "generate requirements document", or "ingest requirements".
version: 0.1.0
---

# Requirements Management

## Overview

To manage functional requirements (FR), technical requirements (TR), test requirements (TEST), and their traceability mappings, use this plugin's declared hook/wrapper (or the REPL transport) for the `workflow.requirements.*` namespace. Do not substitute raw REST calls, generic `PowerShell.MCP wrapper`, helper modules, or another agent's plugin for normal requirements work.

The plugin wrapper validates documented params and emits single-line JSON to REPL stdio. Any direct REPL diagnostic call must use one single-line JSON request envelope, not formatted YAML.

The database is the source of truth for requirements. Markdown files are import/export projections only. Every operation is scoped to the workspace resolved from the signed marker, and generated workspace output must contain only the requested workspace's FR, TR, TEST, and traceability links.

## Initialization

Call `workflow.sessionlog.bootstrap` through this plugin's declared hook/wrapper to initialize the session log subsystem before issuing any workflow commands. This call is idempotent and should be made once per conversation context.

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120000Z-bootstrap-001
  method: workflow.sessionlog.bootstrap
  params: {}
```

## Requirement Scope Layers

Plugin version 1.13.0 and newer exposes native layer operations. Treat this section as the layer API reference when plugin status reports these methods; do not ask the operator or inspect wrapper source just to learn the parameter shapes.

- `workflow.requirements.listLayers` / `req_list_layers` / `client.Requirements.ListRequirementLayersAsync`: omit params.
- `workflow.requirements.createLayer` / `req_create_layer` / `client.Requirements.CreateRequirementLayerAsync`: required params are `key`, `order`, and `name`; optional params are `description` and `scopeEndLayerKey`.
- `workflow.requirements.updateLayer` / `req_update_layer` / `client.Requirements.UpdateRequirementLayerAsync`: required param is `key`; optional params are `name`, `description`, and `scopeEndLayerKey`. Layer `order` is immutable; create a new layer rather than attempting to update `order`.
- `workflow.requirements.effective` / `req_effective` / `client.Requirements.GetEffectiveRequirementsAsync`: optional param is `layerKey`; omit `layerKey` to use the active workspace layer.

Use camelCase exactly in YAML:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T115900Z-listlayers-001
  method: workflow.requirements.listLayers
  params: {}
```

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T115901Z-createlayer-001
  method: workflow.requirements.createLayer
  params:
    key: future
    order: 20
    name: Future Layer
    description: Requirements that are documented but not currently enforceable
```

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T115902Z-updatelayer-001
  method: workflow.requirements.updateLayer
  params:
    key: future
    name: Future Layer
    scopeEndLayerKey: release
```

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T115903Z-effective-001
  method: workflow.requirements.effective
  params:
    layerKey: future
```

FR, TR, TEST, and batch create/update commands also accept requirement scope fields:

- `scopeStartLayerKey`: first layer where the requirement is effective.
- `scopeEndLayerKey`: last layer where the requirement is effective; omit for open-ended scope.

Omit both fields for requirements that are effective in the default/current layer.

## Requirement ID Conventions

Three ID spaces are in use:

- **FR** - Functional Requirements: `^FR-[A-Z]+-\d{3}$`, e.g. `FR-MCP-001`, `FR-AUTH-042`
- **TR** - Technical Requirements: `^TR-[A-Z]+-[A-Z]+-\d{3}$`, e.g. `TR-MCP-ARCH-001`, `TR-AUTH-SEC-002`
- **TEST** - Test Requirements: `^TEST-[A-Z]+-\d{3}$`, e.g. `TEST-MCP-001`, `TEST-AUTH-003`

All IDs must be uppercase. TR IDs require both an area and a subarea segment; FR and TEST IDs require only an area segment.

## Functional Requirements (FR)

### Listing FRs

To retrieve a filtered list of functional requirements:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120000Z-listfr-001
  method: workflow.requirements.listFr
  params:
    area: MCP
    status: in_progress
```

All params are optional; omit to return all FRs. The result contains an `items` array:

```yaml
type: result
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120000Z-listfr-001
  result:
    items:
      - id: FR-MCP-001
        title: Agent authentication
        description: System must authenticate AI agents via API key
        status: completed
        priority: critical
        area: MCP
        createdAt: 2026-03-01T10:00:00Z
        updatedAt: 2026-04-09T12:00:00Z
    totalCount: 1
```

Valid `status` values: `pending`, `in_progress`, `completed`, `deferred`.

### Getting a Single FR

To fetch one functional requirement by ID:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120001Z-getfr-001
  method: workflow.requirements.getFr
  params:
    id: FR-MCP-001
```

### Creating an FR

To record a new functional requirement:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120002Z-createfr-001
  method: workflow.requirements.createFr
  params:
    id: FR-MCP-003
    title: Context search
    description: System must support semantic search across workspace documents
    priority: high
    area: MCP
    notes: Use hybrid search combining BM25 and vector embeddings
```

Required fields: `id`, `title`, `description`, `priority`, `area`. The `notes` field is optional.

### Acceptance Criteria

FR, TR, and TEST create/update commands accept structured `acceptanceCriteria` entries with the same shape used by TODO execution criteria:

```yaml
method: workflow.requirements.createFr
params:
  id: FR-MCP-XXX-001
  title: Acceptance criteria example
  description: Requirement records preserve structured pass/fail criteria.
  priority: high
  area: MCP
  acceptanceCriteria:
    - id: ac-1
      text: Round-trip preserves criterion text
      isSatisfied: false
    - id: ac-2
      text: Evidence is retained when supplied
      isSatisfied: true
      evidence: tests/Services/RequirementAcceptanceCriteriaTests.cs
```

To copy criteria from an execution TODO onto a requirement, call `workflow.requirements.copyAcceptanceCriteriaFromTodo`:

```yaml
method: workflow.requirements.copyAcceptanceCriteriaFromTodo
params:
  kind: fr
  id: FR-MCP-XXX-001
  todoId: PLAN-MCP-001
```

This maps to `POST /mcpserver/requirements/{kind}/{id}/acceptance-criteria/copy-from-todo` with body `{ "todoId": "PLAN-MCP-001" }`.

### Batch Create Or Update

When creating or updating multiple records, prefer the atomic batch commands instead of Markdown ingestion. Batch commands accept YAML `records:` arrays and fail all records if any record is invalid, conflicts, or is missing during update.

Use per-kind commands when every record is the same type:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120002Z-createfr-batch-001
  method: workflow.requirements.createFrBatch
  params:
    records:
      - id: FR-MCP-004
        title: Batch requirements
        description: The system must accept multiple requirement records in one request.
        priority: high
      - id: FR-MCP-005
        title: Atomic validation
        description: The system must reject the whole batch when one record is invalid.
        priority: high
```

Use `workflow.requirements.updateFrBatch`, `createTrBatch`, `updateTrBatch`, `createTestBatch`, and `updateTestBatch` for per-kind batches. For mixed FR/TR/TEST arrays, use `workflow.requirements.createBatch` or `workflow.requirements.updateBatch` and include `kind: fr|tr|test` on each record.

### Updating an FR

To modify an existing FR:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120003Z-updatefr-001
  method: workflow.requirements.updateFr
  params:
    id: FR-MCP-003
    status: completed
    notes: Implemented with HybridSearchService using all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings
```

### Deleting an FR

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120004Z-deletefr-001
  method: workflow.requirements.deleteFr
  params:
    id: FR-MCP-003
```

## Technical Requirements (TR)

TR IDs require both `area` and `subarea` segments. The full ID format is `TR-<AREA>-<SUBAREA>-###`.

### Listing TRs

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120005Z-listtr-001
  method: workflow.requirements.listTr
  params:
    area: MCP
    subarea: PERF
```

### Creating a TR

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120006Z-createtr-001
  method: workflow.requirements.createTr
  params:
    id: TR-MCP-PERF-001
    title: API response time SLA
    description: All API endpoints must respond within 500ms at p99
    priority: high
    area: MCP
    subarea: PERF
    notes: Measured at gateway, excluding network transit time
```

### Updating a TR

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120007Z-updatetr-001
  method: workflow.requirements.updateTr
  params:
    id: TR-MCP-PERF-001
    status: in_progress
    notes: Baseline established at 320ms p99 under load test
```

### Deleting a TR

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120008Z-deletetr-001
  method: workflow.requirements.deleteTr
  params:
    id: TR-MCP-PERF-001
```

## Test Requirements (TEST)

### Listing TEST Requirements

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120009Z-listtest-001
  method: workflow.requirements.listTest
  params:
    area: MCP
```

### Creating a TEST Requirement

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120010Z-createtest-001
  method: workflow.requirements.createTest
  params:
    id: TEST-MCP-001
    title: Agent authentication unit test
    description: Verify API key authentication rejects invalid tokens with 401
    priority: critical
    area: MCP
    notes: Uses in-memory EF provider with CustomWebApplicationFactory
```

### Updating and Deleting TEST Requirements

Follow the same pattern as FR: use `workflow.requirements.updateTest` and `workflow.requirements.deleteTest` with the same parameter shapes.

## Requirement Mappings

Mappings link an FR to one or more TRs and TEST IDs in the current workspace, forming the traceability matrix.

### Listing Mappings

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120011Z-listmap-001
  method: workflow.requirements.listMappings
  params:
    frId: FR-MCP-001
```

### Creating a Mapping

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120012Z-createmap-001
  method: workflow.requirements.createMapping
  params:
    frId: FR-MCP-001
    trIds:
      - TR-MCP-ARCH-001
    testIds:
      - TEST-MCP-001
    notes: Core authentication flow covered by ARCH constraint and unit test
```

Legacy single-link `trId` and `testId` inputs are accepted for compatibility. Prefer `trIds` and `testIds` for all new calls.

The result confirms the stored mapping:

```yaml
type: result
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120012Z-createmap-001
  result:
    item:
      frId: FR-MCP-001
      trId: TR-MCP-ARCH-001
      testId: TEST-MCP-001
      createdAt: 2026-04-09T12:00:12Z
      notes: Core authentication flow covered by ARCH constraint and unit test
```

### Deleting a Mapping

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120013Z-deletemap-001
  method: workflow.requirements.deleteMapping
  params:
    frId: FR-MCP-001
    trId: TR-MCP-ARCH-001
```

## Document Generation

To generate formatted requirements documents from the current workspace database slice:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120014Z-gendoc-001
  method: workflow.requirements.generateDocument
  params:
    format: markdown
    docType: matrix
```

Valid `docType` values:

- `functional` - numbered list of all FR entries with status and description
- `technical` - numbered list of all TR entries grouped by area/subarea
- `testing` - numbered list of all TEST entries with linked FR IDs
- `matrix` - traceability matrix table: FR × TR × TEST × status
- `all` - complete export package

```yaml
type: result
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120014Z-gendoc-001
  result:
    content: |
      # Requirement Traceability Matrix

      | FR ID      | TR ID           | TEST ID      | Status |
      |------------|-----------------|--------------|--------|
      | FR-MCP-001 | TR-MCP-ARCH-001 | TEST-MCP-001 | done   |
      | FR-MCP-002 | TR-MCP-ARCH-002 | TEST-MCP-003 | open   |
    format: markdown
    docType: matrix
    generatedAt: 2026-04-09T12:00:14Z
```

### Wiki Export

Use `format: wiki` with `docType: all` to export wiki files directly into the workspace. The normal result returns metadata, not archive bytes. Files are written under `docs/Project/wiki/azure` and `docs/Project/wiki/github`. Each folder includes `.mcp-requirements-manifest.json`; Azure also includes `.order`; GitHub also includes `_Sidebar.md` and `_Footer.md`. When an older REPL cannot serialize the metadata result, the wrapper may return `contentBase64` with `contentType: application/json`; decode it to read the same export metadata.

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120014Z-gendoc-wiki-001
  method: workflow.requirements.generateDocument
  params:
    format: wiki
    docType: all
```

```yaml
type: result
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120014Z-gendoc-wiki-001
  result:
    format: wiki
    docType: all
    generatedAtUtc: 2026-04-09T12:00:14Z
    outputRoot: F:\GitHub\McpServer\docs\Project\wiki
    files:
      - relativePath: azure/Home.md
        fullPath: F:\GitHub\McpServer\docs\Project\wiki\azure\Home.md
        contentType: text/markdown
        lastModifiedUtc: 2026-04-09T12:00:14Z
```

## Bulk Ingestion

To import requirements from an existing Markdown document:

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120015Z-ingest-001
  method: workflow.requirements.ingestDocument
  params:
    content: |
      ## FR-MCP-010: GraphRAG ingestion
      The system must support ingestion of raw text into the GraphRAG corpus.
      Priority: high | Area: MCP | Status: pending

      ## TR-MCP-GRAPH-001: Chunked text embedding
      Ingested text must be split into chunks and embedded using all-MiniLM-L6-v2.
      Priority: high | Area: MCP | Subarea: GRAPH | Status: pending
    format: markdown
```

To import wiki documents, pass a path-keyed `documents` map and include `lastModifiedUtc` per entry when available. Use `sourceFormat: auto` or `wiki`; set `preferredWikiFormat: azure|github` only when the Azure and GitHub timestamp checks disagree. The server compares both `.mcp-requirements-manifest.json` `generatedAtUtc` values and the latest `lastModifiedUtc` per platform. If both checks agree, the newer platform is selected. If they disagree and no preference is supplied, import fails. The selected platform folder is authoritative: missing records are deleted, changed records are updated, new records are created, and identical records are ignored.

```yaml
type: request
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120015Z-ingest-wiki-001
  method: workflow.requirements.ingestDocument
  params:
    format: wiki
    sourceFormat: wiki
    preferredWikiFormat: github
    documents:
      github/.mcp-requirements-manifest.json:
        content: '{"generatedAtUtc":"2026-04-09T12:00:14Z"}'
        lastModifiedUtc: 2026-04-09T12:00:14Z
      github/Functional-Requirements.md:
        content: |
          # Functional Requirements (MCP Server)
        lastModifiedUtc: 2026-04-09T12:00:15Z
```

The server parses the document, creates, updates, deletes, or ignores matching FR/TR/TEST/mapping records, and returns a summary:

```yaml
type: result
payload:
  requestId: req-20260409T120015Z-ingest-001
  result:
    created: 2
    updated: 0
    skipped: 0
    errors: []
```

## Error Handling

Common error codes:

- `requirement_not_found` - no requirement with the given ID
- `requirement_already_exists` - ID already in use; update instead of create
- `invalid_requirement_id` - ID does not match the expected regex for its type
- `mapping_not_found` - mapping between the specified FR and TR does not exist
- `invalid_mapping` - mapping references a non-existent FR, TR, or TEST ID
- `document_generation_error` - failed to render the requested document format
- `document_ingestion_error` - could not parse or persist the ingested document

## Workflow Recommendations

When discovering or agreeing on new requirements during a session:

1. Create the FR record immediately using `workflow.requirements.createFr`
2. Create the corresponding TR records using `workflow.requirements.createTr`
3. Create the TEST record using `workflow.requirements.createTest`
4. Link them with `workflow.requirements.createMapping`
5. Include the new IDs in the session log turn tags via `workflow.sessionlog.updateTurn`

Capture requirements as they emerge; do not defer to end of session. Requirements traceability is validated in CI and build failures result from missing mappings.

Import-McpYamlSerializer
$bom = [string][char]0xFEFF
$sessionId = 'ClaudeCode-20261029T010023Z-plugin-session'
$requestId = 'req-20261029T010106Z-hv-admin-pwa-source-round1'
$raw = & $wrapper -Command Invoke -Method 'workflow.sessionlog.queryHistory' -ParamsObject ([ordered]@{ agent = 'ClaudeCode'; limit = 5; offset = 0 }) -WorkspacePath $ws -PluginRoot $plugin 2>$null
$text = ($raw | Out-String).Replace($bom, '')
$text = [regex]::Replace($text, '(?i)(api[_-]?key["'':\s=]+)[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{20,}', '$1<redacted>')

    }
}
Write-Output ("RECEIPT {0} sha256={1}" -f $receipt, (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $receipt -Algorithm SHA256).Hash)

# Hostile validation verdict: admin PWA candidate `437c501c`

**OverallVerdict: DISAGREE.** Accuracy 92, completeness 88. Both are below 98, and surfaces 1, 2 and 3 each have a FAIL. The candidate is **not ready for staging** until F1 is fixed and you decide F2 and F3.

- **Reviewed revision:** `437c501c58c7dfa96ee576f445d225f2dd62a0bd` (base `8e2f6241`). It is HEAD and the tracked tree is clean.
- **Reviewer model:** `claude-opus-5-5`, verified from the init event at response.jsonl line 7.
- **Reviewer effort:** "high" comes only from the launch command. The init event reports `per_turn_effort_active:true` with no value, so effort is not verified at runtime.
- **Plugin:** version 1.121.0 according to its own manifest. The marker still lists 1.26.0, which is an out-of-date marker field.
- **Counts:** 31 PASS, 4 FAIL, 3 UNKNOWN, out of 38 items.
- **Classes:** the source, tests, docs and QBrain changes are product implementation work. The GitHub App registration is an operator-directed provider operation and is scored separately.

## What holds (observed, with receipts)
- **GitHub provider:** only numeric ID 16146732 with login `sharpninja` can sign in. It uses S256 PKCE and state, requests no scopes, and keeps no provider tokens (`src/infrastructure/github-admin.ts:9-105`).
- **Guest/admin separation:** admin session hashes carry a `github-admin` prefix, and the guest service is guest-only (`identity.ts:137-164`, `admin-session.ts:6-16`). Copying a token into the other cookie fails in both directions against real PostgreSQL (`admin.integration.ts:485-552`).
- **Public routes:** the old OpenAI routes, user delegation and community routes are closed. `nominate` is reachable only through the admin-gated `/api/content`.
- **Admin PWA:** the worker handles only admin page navigations and caches only the offline page plus 4 icons. Retiring the old public worker removes only that worker and its own caches.
- **UI fixes:** stale-response races are guarded, the card padding gives 20px on phones and 32px on desktop, and the presence-timer fix is correct.
- **Test evidence:** all 5 TRX files match the request hashes and counts (582/69/68/13/1). Each matches its native JUnit case by case, in order, with 0 failed and 0 skipped. All 60 unit test files are present.

## FAIL items
- **S1-23 and S3-04 (finding F1, high, product):** the verified GitHub owner's profile is created public and shown on the public leaderboard and landing page, with no way to opt out.
  - The admin profile is created as a "member", and every member profile starts public (`identity.ts:100`, `identity.ts:221-227`).
  - The public leaderboard query returns the id and alias of every public profile (`002_public_reads.sql:22-24`).
  - The admin UI hides the profile preferences (`identity-panel.tsx:210`), and `/api/profile` only accepts guest sessions, so the owner cannot turn it off.
  - This contradicts DEC-11 ("users can... opt out of leaderboard display"), which is marked satisfied on FR-PLAYERPROFILE-002, and GA-01 (guest-only public play).
  - The 19:32 PostgreSQL run failed TR-30 with exactly one extra public row (`run-history/guest-admin-postgres.log:225-243`). The next green run followed test cleanup, and no product analysis was recorded. That the extra row was the owner profile is my inference from its id format.
- **S2-05 (F2, medium, process):** there is no documented BDPv4 green mock gate and no chronological receipts for this slice (`self-review.json:46`). This finding is based on the missing receipt, not on FR timestamps.
- **S3-03 (F3, medium, traceability):** no TR or TEST record carries GA-09, your card-whitespace request. GA-05, GA-06 and GA-07 are also on no TR or TEST record, and they restate PWA criteria under second IDs (GA-06 is word-for-word PWA-09).

## UNKNOWN items
- **S1-06 (F4):** the adapter's fixture validation exists only as a bare summary (`trx-adapter-validation.json`). The adapter's hash does match the committed script.
- **S1-10 (F5):** `pwa.spec.ts` was edited at 19:46:11, after the full browser run ended at 19:45:10. Only the card case was rerun on the committed version.
- **S4-04:** the GitHub App registration and its callback URLs can't be verified from the repository. This is a provider operation still to be observed at staging.

## Missing tests and decisions
1. **F1 acceptance criterion:** add "GA-10: the owner profile is non-public and never appears in public listings."
   - Tests to add: a unit test that the owner's new profile is non-public; a PostgreSQL test that public listings exclude the owner after sign-in, without relying on cleanup order; a browser test that the public board shows no member alias.
   - **Your decision:** whether older member profiles from the retired OpenAI sign-in should also be hidden from public listings.
2. **F2, your decision:** accept a documented BDPv4 exception for this slice, or require a retroactive mock-gate evidence package.
3. **F3:** put GA-09 on a TEST record, naming `pwa.spec.ts:118` and `pwa-support.test.ts:139` as its cases. Then either map GA-05/06/07 onto TEST criteria or replace them with references to the matching PWA criteria.
4. **F4:** keep the adapter validation script, its fixtures and its output.
5. **F5:** supply a run of all four `pwa.spec.ts` cases on the committed version.

## Informational
- **F6:** QBrain record reads return the time of the read as createdAt/updatedAt. I filed this as `triage-report-618a93a51dd54d92b620dba566f21bfb`. It confirms that FR timestamps can't support chronology.
- **F7:** three `it.each` groups produce duplicate test names, so their TRX rows can't be told apart by name.
- **F8:** hook enforcement is unverified. The plugin root variable isn't set for this source plugin. The hook-opened turn `req-20261029T005811Z-prompt-88ee` lives in a separate session (`ClaudeCode-20261029T005806Z-plugin-session`), still in progress with 1 turn. I opened a dedicated review turn instead.

## Receipts and persistence
- **Profile load:** 1 profile file, 3 Global memories, and 0 Workspace memories (verified `totalCount=0`). PRIVATE-MEMORY-REFERENCE-007 was filtered out before anything was shown.
- **Verdict JSON:** `docs/receipts/hv/20261028T195803-admin-pwa-source-round1.verdict.json` (SHA-256 `DCD8AA22B33EE794404FEA7044404B26025E14051FF24D2D3F251DA7E8BBECDC`).
- **Request and response streams:** the `.request.jsonl` and `.response.jsonl` files alongside it. The response stream redacts the marker key.
- **MCP turn:** `ClaudeCode-20261029T010023Z-plugin-session` / `req-20261029T010106Z-hv-admin-pwa-source-round1`, linked to parent `Codex-20261027T100516Z-plugin-session` / `req-20261029T000126Z-prompt-ee7f`.
- **Persistence proof:** a live `client.SessionLog.QueryAsync` read (request `req-20261029T011527Z-c150`) returns the turn as `completed`. It has 6 dialog items, and its 5 verdict JSON parts reassemble byte-identical to the file. It also holds 49 actions (47 design decisions), and the response contains "OverallVerdict DISAGREE" plus the receipt paths. Saved as `docs/receipts/hv/claude-opus-round1-tools/session-turn-proof.yaml` (SHA-256 `800C05AA…2CEA37`).
- **What I wrote:** only files under `docs/receipts/hv/`, plus the plugin's own cache and the triage report. No builds, tests, product edits or git changes.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- **How admin access works:** the app runs the same identity service twice, and the admin copy prefixes every token hash with `github-admin`. Copied cookies therefore fail cleanly. The catch is that both copies create profiles the same way, so the admin inherited the "members start public" default meant for the retired OpenAI sign-in.
- **The test failure was the clue:** the 19:32 TR-30 failure was the test suite detecting F1. Cleaning up test data made it green, but the product behaviour is unchanged. Retaining failed runs is what made this visible.
- **Checking the converted TRX files:** the adapter's own validation was only a bare summary. Matching each TRX case by case against its original JUnit, and checking the embedded hash, tests the adapter on the real data directly.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Accuracy rating: 95, because every claim above is anchored to a file, a command output or a live query. The one inference (that the extra public row was the owner's profile) is labelled. Completeness rating: 96, because I covered all four surfaces and every named requirement record. I did not look inside the unchanged realtime and live-only test lanes.
